subject: Subprocessor provenance and incident-runbook synchronization
body:
From: Mike Truong <mike.truong@archfield.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Archfield Security Team <security@archfield.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: subprocessor provenance + incident-runbook mapping

Hi Ben / Laura,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our procurement security review we need a clear mapping of Redwood's active subprocessors (production-facing) and a short runbook that describes:
- who owns incident response for incidents involving each subprocessor,
- where encryption keys are hosted (KMS provider + region), and
- whether any subproc processes unredacted customer data.

Can you send a CSV roster and an example runbook snippet (we just need the template you use to map responsibilities)? Also let us know if you can provide a snapshot of KMS residency (which clouds/regions hold key material) for the subprocessors handling inference and telemetry.

Target: we need an evidence package for our SIG+CAIQ intake by 2026-11-24. If there are parts you can’t share publicly, please flag them and propose an alternative (e.g., redacted artifact plus attestation).

Appreciate it — Mike

--
Mike Truong
Security Operations Lead
Archfield Therapeutics

[Attachment: archfield-evidence-ask.pdf (PDF)]

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mike Truong <mike.truong@archfield.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor provenance + incident-runbook mapping

Mike — thanks for the clear ask. We can provide the roster and the runbook template. High level plan: 
1) Deliver a CSV roster with active subprocessors and primary contact, data scopes, and whether they process unredacted data.
2) Provide a KMS residency snapshot for keys used in inference and telemetry.
3) Attach our internal incident-runbook mapping doc (redacted where necessary) and a short attestation on items we cannot publish.

I’m attaching the initial roster (see filename below). Laura, Naomi — would you be able to take the KMS snapshot and incident ownership mapping? I’ve tentatively scheduled an internal sync on Wednesday to finalize the bundle.

Proposed delivery to Archfield: 2026-11-23 (gives us a day buffer before your 11/24 target). If that works for you, we’ll upload to the shared Drive and send a DocuSign attestation for any redacted elements.

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

[Attachment: redwood-subproc-roster-v1.csv (CSV)]

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mike Truong <mike.truong@archfield.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor provenance + incident-runbook mapping

Thanks Ben & Mike — quick clarifications before we produce the bundle: 

Questions / notes: 
- Scope: we'll include only subprocessors with production access to customer data (inference, embeddings, telemetry). Internal vendors (payroll, HR) will be explicitly excluded.
- KMS: for inference keys we use HSM-backed KMS in our primary US region (us-west-2) and a cross-region replica in eu-west-1 for failover. We will provide a snapshot labeled with key IDs and hosting region but not the key material.
- Incident ownership: we map primary (Redwood) and secondary (subprocessor) contacts and include SLAs and escalation paths. For any subprocessor under a data processing agreement that prevents sharing contact details, we'll include an attestation and redaction note.

Attachments I’ll add to the bundle: incident-runbook-mapping.docx (runbook template with redaction markers) and kms_provenance_snapshot.xlsx (key IDs + region metadata). I’ll also seed the Drive folder listed below.

Delivery timeline: we’ll aim to publish the Drive folder and a single ZIP evidence bundle by Mon 11/22 EOD; Ben will push the DocuSign attestation link if needed. If Archfield needs earlier access to any specific artifacts, flag which items and we’ll prioritize.

Laura Bennett
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

[Attachments: incident-runbook-mapping.docx (DOCX), kms_provenance_snapshot.xlsx (XLSX)]

Related drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-subproc
JIRA: JIRA-SEC-4721

---

From: Mike Truong <mike.truong@archfield.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor provenance + incident-runbook mapping

Laura / Ben — this looks good, thank you. 11/22 EOD for the Drive bundle is acceptable; please include the attestation language for the redacted fields so our SIG reviewer has context. Also confirm whether your runbook includes:
- an example timeline for containment + notification (hours),
- whether Redwood initiates forensic collection for subprocessor incidents or requires the subprocessor to deliver artifacts, and
- point of contact escalation for cross-border data residency cases.

If you can include short answers to those three in the cover README we’ll be able to close our intake faster. Otherwise happy to set a 30-min call next week.

Best — Mike

[Archfield Security Team]
